key_insight: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model that can listen and speak at the same time while also calling tools natively. It unifies transcription, reasoning, function calling, and streaming speech generation in one real-time system.
problem_solved: Traditional voice assistants often handle speech input and output in separate, sequential steps, which creates latency and makes natural turn-taking harder. This paper addresses the challenge of building a single streaming model that can understand user speech, generate responses, and invoke tools simultaneously.
method: Uses a streaming speech encoder paired with a decoder-only language model for real-time understanding and reasoning.
Adds parallel output streams for agent text and structured function calls to support native tool calling.
Includes an auxiliary RNN-T branch for incremental user transcription and a streaming TTS decoder for low-latency speech output.
impact: This matters because it brings agents closer to natural human conversation: faster responses, smoother interruptions, and more capable voice interfaces. For practitioners, it provides an open architecture for building real-time spoken assistants that can both talk and act.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing speech input -> transcription -> reasoning -> tool call -> spoken output.

Icons for microphone, brain/LLM, wrench/tool, and speaker to map each subsystem.
paper_title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
paper_authors: Jagadeesh Balam, Travis Bartley, Edresson Casanova, Sanjay Chauhan, Chen Chen
